audit_findings.title: FY2025 owner earnings may retain an expired 1% financing cost
audit_findings.magnitude: $13.516 million annual pre-tax, approximately $10.002 million after the filed 26% interim tax rate
audit_findings.mechanism: The equity-level OE numerator retains interest expense, so replacing the $360 million 2026 Notes with revolving-credit borrowings changes recurring OE and every forecast and terminal year.
audit_findings.evidence: In the future, we expect to use the available capacity under the Credit Facility for any payments made in connection with any settlement of the 2026 Notes upon conversion, redemption, or repayment of our 2026 Notes at or prior to the 2026 Notes maturity.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated temporal mismatch, not merely a possibility. The May 2026 filing confirms that the notes were redeemed with revolving-credit borrowings. At the filed 5.37% revolver rate, $360 million costs $19.332 million annually versus the notes' $5.816 million FY2025 effective interest cost, a $13.516 million pre-tax increase. The approximately $10.002 million after-tax reduction equals 4.7% of the $212 million anchor and is amplified through the terminal value, making it reasonably capable of materially changing the valuation margin.
audit_findings.action: Normalize the anchor to post-redemption interest using the actual revolving-credit balance and rate at the valuation date, apply the appropriate ongoing cash-tax effect, and rerun all scenarios and the buy-below price.

audit_findings.title: The convertible-note shares and earnings numerator describe different claims
audit_findings.magnitude: 6.643 million shares, 12.7% of the 52.19 million-share denominator
audit_findings.mechanism: The denominator dilutes value per share while the OE numerator continues to bear 2030 Notes interest and the cash-settled principal claim.
audit_findings.evidence: However, because the principal amount will be settled in cash, the dilutive impact of applying the if-converted method is limited to the in-the-money portion, if any.
audit_findings.explanation: The inconsistency is demonstrated. The filing says principal will be cash-settled and that dilution is limited to any in-the-money conversion premium, yet the valuation includes approximately all 6.643 million shares initially underlying the 2030 Notes. At the $44.05 valuation price the $67.74 conversion price is out of the money, and the May 2026 filing reported no note dilution. Including the entire block reduces every stated per-share value by using claims that cannot simultaneously coexist with the interest-bearing, cash-settled treatment. The block is large enough to materially affect the per-share valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild the share count from 41.013 million June 2026 common shares plus applicable equity-award dilution and only scenario-specific in-the-money conversion-premium shares; alternatively use a fully consistent if-converted numerator and denominator, then rerun all scenarios and the buy-below price.

audit_findings.title: Serial-acquisition capital consumption may be missing from owner earnings
audit_findings.mechanism: Potentially omitted acquisition or replacement capital affects normalized OE, while acquisition-driven historical growth may also be embedded in the forecast growth rate without the capital required to produce it.
audit_findings.evidence: Our capital allocation policy emphasizes accretive M&A, which we believe allows us to expand our business and drive significant stockholder returns.
audit_findings.explanation: The acquisition-led strategy and $145.492 million of FY2025 acquired-intangible amortization are demonstrated, but the economically required replacement or acquisition capital is unresolved. The amortization equals 68.6% of the $212 million anchor, so an unrestricted add-back paired with acquisition-derived growth could materially overstate earning power. Amortization itself is not automatically a cash cost, and the filings do not establish the amount of recurring capital necessary; therefore the valuation error remains unquantified.
audit_findings.action: Produce the complete $212 million OE reconciliation, identify each amortization add-back, measure same-perimeter revenue and OE growth excluding acquired businesses, and rerun growth and OE using a filed or otherwise supportable recurring acquisition/replacement-capital charge.

audit_findings.title: MOVEit creates an unrecorded claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.mechanism: An uninsured judgment, settlement, indemnification payment, fine, or defense cost would reduce the equity bridge or future OE before value reaches common shareholders.
audit_findings.evidence: Therefore, we have not recorded a loss contingency liability for the MOVEit Vulnerability as of November 30, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The exposure is unresolved rather than a demonstrated valuation error. The May 2026 filing says a loss is reasonably possible but cannot estimate a range, no contingency liability is recorded, and only $1.1 million of insurance remained. Net MOVEit costs already filed total $12.524 million through May 2026, but those costs do not quantify the outstanding claims. The record therefore cannot establish whether the unrecorded exposure is large enough to change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Update the MDL through the valuation date, including class-certification developments, customer and insurer claims, regulatory matters, defense-cost run rate, and remaining insurance; deduct a supportable probability-weighted uninsured liability from the bridge and normalize recurring legal costs in OE.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may contain a nonrecurring tax benefit
audit_findings.magnitude: $7.5 million; computed maximum base-value effect approximately $124.3 million or $2.38 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: If retained, the one-time tax benefit increases anchor OE and consequently all forecast and terminal cash flows.
audit_findings.evidence: In fiscal year 2025, the Company recorded a tax benefit of $7.5 million as a result of a change in the Company’s estimate of its deferred tax liability associated with unremitted foreign earnings.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the benefit was retained is unresolved, but its isolated materiality is bounded by the filed $7.5 million amount. Treating the full amount as an anchor overstatement equals 3.54% of OE and proportionally reduces the $3.514 billion base operating PV by about $124.3 million, or $2.38 per share. The base value would remain about $66.93 per share and the 30% buy-below level about $46.85, still above the $44.05 price. On the supplied numbers, this item alone does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Verify the anchor reconciliation removes the $7.5 million benefit and uses an ongoing cash-tax rate; if not, reduce FY2025 OE by the retained amount and rerun the scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Gross cash may not be distributable net of repatriation tax
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $7.9 million, approximately $0.15 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds gross cash and short-term investments; any unpaid tax necessary to repatriate foreign cash should reduce the cash added to common equity.
audit_findings.evidence: At November 30, 2025, we maintain a deferred tax liability of $7.9 million for the U.S. federal, state, and foreign withholding taxes expected to be imposed upon the repatriation of unremitted foreign earnings that are not considered indefinitely reinvested.
audit_findings.explanation: The November 2025 filing records a $7.9 million deferred tax liability for expected repatriation taxes, while $70.0 million of the May 2026 cash balance was held abroad. Even assuming the entire filed liability must be deducted separately from the bridge, the effect is only about $0.15 per share, or roughly $0.11 on the 30%-discount buy-below price. That scale cannot change the supplied valuation conclusion. Whether some or all is already reflected through deferred-tax accounting still requires reconciliation.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the May 2026 cash-by-jurisdiction schedule and deferred-tax roll-forward, identify the unpaid tax specifically associated with cash included in the bridge, and deduct only the amount not already captured elsewhere.
